ov: Eight species of small, dolphin-like toothed whales, more closely related to narwhals and belugas than to dolphins. They have spade-shaped teeth and no pronounced beak, find their way mainly by echolocation, and keep warm with a layer of blubber.

why.et: The Inuit hunt harbour porpoises, and a drive hunt for Dall's porpoise continues in Japan.

rg: Rivers, coasts and open ocean, in waters from tropical (the vaquita, in the Sea of Cortez) to polar (the harbour porpoise, off Greenland).
df: Mainly fish from the seabed and open water; also squid, shrimp and krill.

cf.tip: Porpoises have spade-shaped teeth and no pronounced beak; dolphins have cone-shaped teeth.

fx: The vaquita, the smallest porpoise, is one of the smallest toothed whales.
In several species the females are larger than the males.
